method: One uniform pathway-level interpretation pass over all 16 final ranked pathways. Every record uses the same evidence contract: the official pathway definition, exact input intersection genes, Alzheimer's disease interpretation and pathway-attached PubMed records.

GO:0150076.cell_context: Most relevant to plaque-associated microglia and reactive astrocytes in hippocampal and cortical regions, where sustained innate-immune signaling, cytokine release and oxidative injury can amplify synaptic damage in Alzheimer's disease; infiltrating myeloid cells may contribute, but the resident glial context is primary.

GO:0001774.cell_context: Specific to microglia, particularly plaque-associated and disease-associated microglial states in hippocampus and cortex, where phagocytic, lysosomal and inflammatory programs alter amyloid-beta handling and synaptic homeostasis.

GO:0006954.cell_context: Most relevant to activated microglia and reactive astrocytes in Alzheimer's disease-affected hippocampal and cortical tissue, with possible contribution from peripheral myeloid cells; this broad term is not restricted to a single brain cell type.

GO:0061900.cell_context: Most relevant to reactive microglia and astrocytes in plaque- and tau-affected hippocampal and cortical regions, where spatially organized glial state changes track neuroinflammatory progression and tissue injury.

GO:0005515.cell_context: This broad molecular function spans multiple compartments and has no unique cell-type assignment. In Alzheimer's disease it is most pertinent to neuronal synapses and axons and to glial cells, including microglia, where protein-interaction networks regulate tau and amyloid binding, clearance and inflammatory signaling.

GO:0005509.cell_context: Most relevant to excitatory pyramidal neurons and their hippocampal and cortical synapses, where calcium-binding proteins regulate neurotransmitter release, plasticity and stress signaling. In Alzheimer's disease, calcium dyshomeostasis is particularly consequential in vulnerable neuronal populations.

GO:0005764.cell_context: Most relevant to cortical and hippocampal neurons, plaque-associated microglia and reactive astrocytes. Neuronal lysosomes clear amyloid-beta, tau and damaged organelles, whereas glial lysosomes support plaque uptake and inflammatory-cargo processing.

GO:0005783.cell_context: Most relevant to cortical and hippocampal neurons with high secretory and calcium-handling demands, with additional roles in reactive astrocytes. Chronic endoplasmic-reticulum stress in these cells can couple proteostasis failure and calcium imbalance to inflammatory and apoptotic signaling.

GO:0005788.cell_context: Most relevant to cortical and hippocampal pyramidal neurons, where APP, synaptic receptors and neuropeptides impose high secretory-pathway demand. Luminal folding stress in these neurons can compromise proteostasis and increase vulnerability to Alzheimer's disease pathology.

KEGG:04142.cell_context: Most relevant to neurons, microglia and astrocytes in hippocampal and cortical regions. Neuronal lysosome biogenesis supports autophagic clearance of amyloid-beta, tau and damaged organelles, whereas glial lysosomes support plaque uptake and inflammatory-cargo processing.

KEGG:04210.cell_context: Most relevant to vulnerable hippocampal and association-cortex neurons undergoing amyloid-, tau-, excitotoxic- and metabolic-stress signaling. Astrocytes and microglia may also engage apoptotic programs during chronic neuroinflammation, but neuronal loss is the principal disease-defining context.

REAC:R-HSA-168249.cell_context: Primarily maps to brain-resident microglia in plaque- and tau-affected cortex and hippocampus, with additional roles for astrocytes and infiltrating monocytes and macrophages. These cells execute pattern recognition, cytokine signaling, phagocytosis and immune-linked cell death in Alzheimer's disease.

GO:0006979.cell_context: Most relevant to vulnerable hippocampal and cortical neurons exposed to mitochondrial and proteotoxic stress, and to astrocytes and microglia that regulate antioxidant support and inflammatory reactive-oxygen-species production in Alzheimer's disease tissue.

GO:0043065.cell_context: Most relevant to vulnerable neurons in hippocampus and association cortex undergoing amyloid-, tau- and stress-associated death signaling; cerebral pericytes and inflammatory glia may also engage pro-death programs in vascular and neuroinflammatory niches.

GO:0006457.cell_context: Most relevant to cortical and hippocampal neurons with high APP, tau and synaptic-protein proteostatic load, with supporting roles in astrocytes and microglia that manage extracellular and intracellular aggregates and cellular stress responses.

GO:0002526.cell_context: Most relevant to acutely activated microglia and reactive astrocytes in injured Alzheimer's disease brain tissue, with additional contributions from infiltrating myeloid cells and circulating acute-phase programs; because the term is broad, it is not specific to resident central-nervous-system cells.
